You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

{
 "action": "create",
 "name": "continual-arc-horizontal-vertical-bridges",
 "content": "---
name: continual-arc-horizontal-vertical-bridges
description: Use when an ARC grid has segmented horizontal bars and matching single-cell gaps aligned with vertical stems. Extend the gap columns between bars and preserve/fill the lower stem.
---

# Segmented bars with vertical gap columns

Use this rule when a grid contains horizontal runs that are interrupted by single zero cells, with each interrupted column forming a vertical channel. The examples show horizontal bars at several rows, and sometimes isolated vertical colored pixels near the bottom.

## Transformation

1. Find horizontal rows containing repeated-color runs interrupted by a one-cell zero gap. The gap column is a vertical channel. Fill that gap cell with the common color of the adjacent horizontal runs.
2. Extend the channel vertically through the blank space between such horizontal bars. Each horizontal bar row supplies its own color for that row and the vertical interval until the next bar-row crossing. Preserve all unrelated cells.
3. Do not stop at the lowest horizontal bar: where a vertical colored stem/pixel exists below it, extend that stem’s color through the blank cells between the lowest bar and the bottom anchor, and preserve the anchor. Example: stems at row 14, columns 3 and 8 with colors 6 and 8; after filling horizontal gap channels down through row 11, fill rows 12–14 at those columns with 6 and 8 respectively.
4. A vertical channel may occur at a different column from another, and its active bars may be on different rows. Treat each channel independently. Some input rows may have more than one interrupted bar/gap.
5. The horizontal bars and their existing cells remain unchanged; only fill the aligned blank channel cells, including the lower stem extension.
